name: Hold a commanded ride height
note: Sit, stand, crouch, sneak, squeeze under, crawl and rear up are all one number the command vector does not have.

name: Pitch, roll and yaw the body with the feet planted
note: Bowing, stretching, shaking, leaning and scanning are attitude commands rather than rates; old row 6 gave +/- 20 deg and old row 7 gave +/- 25 deg, so the dial is widened to cover both.

name: Address one leg on its own
note: A three-legged stance, a diagonal pair or one leg held out needs a per-foot command, and nothing in vx, vy, yaw addresses one leg.

name: Lift a foot and hold it up
note: Feet come off the ground because the gait reward makes them, not because anyone asks.

name: Turn in place
note: Slow, fast, and stopping on an exact angle are the same yaw command.

name: Turn where the ground or the space is against it
note: Turning on ice or in a gap 1.1 times the body length is the same command with the world turned up.

name: Walk forward at a commanded speed
note: Stepping in place is this command at zero and holding the line for 3 m is R1's existing drift bar, so idle sway at zero command is not a separate skill.

name: Walk backward, sideways and diagonally - the whole command box
note: Measured on run 25: backward walked 0.00 m in 8 s and pure sideways 3 cm, because WALK_SPEED is 0.15 to 0.35 and vx is never zero or negative.

name: Start, stop and reverse hard
note: Instant start, a dead stop from a sprint and a 180 at full speed are step changes in the same command.

name: Walk a constant arc
note: A constant speed plus a constant turn rate is a circle, a figure eight is two of them flown back to back and turning at speed is the same pair held at 80 % of top, so the radius dial is widened to span every old row.

name: Named gaits
note: Static crawl, pace, amble and backward trot are contact patterns the gait reward already shapes; the gaits with a flight phase are parked.

name: Switch gait mid-walk
note: Changing gait is a speed change, not a new policy.

name: Step on command, one step at a time
note: One step per command, at a commanded rhythm.

name: Step over a low object
note: A rug edge, a cable or a 40 mm block is felt through the leg on contact rather than seen, which is why old row 99 filing the same event as blocked on a camera was wrong; PLAN 5.2 notes range finders reach the anticipating half of it, and the dial spans all three old ranges.

name: Place a foot on a chosen spot
note: Hitting a mark, a stepping stone or the next stair but one needs to see where the spot is, and range finders give range, not a foot-placement map.

name: Probe the ground before committing weight
note: Tapping and scraping before loading a foot fall out of the contact rewards.

name: Pivot, cross over, and brace on a wall
note: A wall is felt through the leg when it pushes against it, the same way a low obstacle already is.

name: Reverse out of a tight place
note: Backing out of a corner, a dead end or a 50 mm gap is what a human on the sticks is for.

name: Drive to a point and stop on a heading
note: The pilot decides where the point is, which heading to stop on, and how to line up on a doorway.

name: Descend a steep slope
note: A steep slope is terrain, a dial in the scene, and going down it backward is just a command.

name: Get up from any ground pose
note: Belly, either side, fully upside down and rolling through the side are one reward with one fixed goal - get upright.

name: Get up on a slope or in a tight space
note: The same reward with the floor tilted or the ceiling at 1.2 times body height.

name: Power on in an unknown pose
note: Powering on in a random joint pose, upside down, mid-air or with a foot trapped all land in R2's start distribution.

name: Picked up and set down elsewhere
note: Being set down is felt through the IMU and lands in an unknown pose, so it is a getting-up start and needs no eyes.

name: Survive a drop
note: Four old rows each named one drop height; the height is a dial, not four skills.

name: Land badly
note: Landing on blocks or a slope, or already rotating, is the same drop with the start state turned up.

name: Recover from a slip, or choose to fall safely
note: A foot sliding out mid-walk and an unrecoverable state are the two ends of the same reward.

name: Use a foot on an object
note: Pushing, dragging, pressing, kicking, digging and pawing all score the object rather than the robot, and PLAN.md shelves this with no trigger to un-shelve.

name: Push while standing
note: Light, hard and hardest are the same impulse with the number raised, from any direction and contact point.

name: Push while walking
note: The same shove, delivered while the feet are moving.

name: Sustained lean or a long push
note: A lean held for 10 s and a push held for 30 s are one sustained force.

name: A sharp tug or a kicked leg
note: A tether yank and a sideways impulse into the swing leg are sharp, not sustained.

name: Low friction underfoot
note: Ice, wet tile, a puddle, worn feet and the ground yanked away are one number, and friction 0.4 is already inside the 0.4 to 1.2 band randomised on every attempt today.

name: Grass, gravel and rubble
note: The policy never sees the word gravel, it sees the same numbers arriving in a different pattern.

name: Ground the foot sinks into
note: Sand and mud differ from gravel by letting the foot go down before it stops.

name: Uneven ground - blocks, gaps, a beam, a rug edge
note: Flat hard floor is the baseline everything else is measured against rather than a skill, and the rest of these are one roughness dial.

name: A surface that moves under it
note: A treadmill is a test rig rather than a skill, and a see-saw and a loose plank are the same tilt dial.

name: Step into an unseen hole
note: An unseen hole is exactly that - felt, not seen.

name: Slopes, up, down and across
note: Up, down and cross-slope are one terrain dial.

name: A curb or single tall step
note: A curb is the stair dial with one step in it.

name: Stairs, up and down
note: Human stairs at a standard rise, forward or backward.

name: Stairs with a load or a dead servo
note: Stairs are the hard case for every other dial, so the load and the dead servo get a row on top of it.

name: Payload
note: Centred, off-centre to 50 mm, sloshing or changing mid-walk, it is one mass dial.

name: Weak, dead or under-powered servos
note: One weak, two weak, one dead per joint in turn, or a flat battery are all reduced torque.

name: Get up under load or on bad ground
note: Getting up on gravel or a slope carrying 2 kg is R2 with D1's dials turned up, not a new skill.

name: Foot wedged or legs tangled
note: Wedged, tangled or standing on its own foot is a scene condition the policy has to survive.

name: Walled in, or walking into a wall
note: Chair legs and a wall are the same condition seen from outside.

name: Handled, tugged and blown sideways
note: A leash tug, a hand on the back and a gust are all sideways force.

name: Trip at speed, or anything else mid-walk
note: Anything carries no information and mostly it is a shove, and tripping at speed is a disturbance rather than a speed measurement.

name: Sensor noise, drift and command delay
note: IMU bias to 2 deg, noise to 3x nominal and up to 100 ms of lag are simulator honesty, not damage.

name: An impossible order
note: How it behaves when asked for a blocked path or an unreachable pose is a property of every run, not a run.

name: Quiet running and a power-save lock
note: Quiet is a penalty on effort rather than something measured afterwards, and power-save is a state rather than a movement.

name: Startup joint sweep
note: Every joint driven through its full range before anything else runs.

name: Fall, get up, keep walking
note: PLAN step 3's handover test - R2 stands it up, hands over, R1 walks 5 m, 100 times with no stall and no fall-loop.

name: Chain moves without stopping
note: Sprint-stop-turn-sprint, stairs to flat to stairs, a friction change mid-stride, a freeze and resume, and an emergency stop are read off, never trained.

name: Top speed and the speed ladder
note: Raise the command until it fails and write down where, per surface, per direction and per payload.

name: Acceleration and a sustained run
note: Zero to top speed, then hold 80 % of it, then keep walking for ten minutes.

name: Smoothness, read off the trained policy
note: Efficient gait at each speed, the same quality on a flat battery, and keeping an object on its back are numbers read off a policy rather than trained toward.

name: Jumping
note: Every contact-gated reward term returns zero the moment all four feet leave the ground, so the airborne part needs its own reward and its own run; PLAN.md un-parks it when stage 3.3 measures real servo speed under load.

name: Seeing
note: A camera the policy itself reads, plus a depth-to-heightmap pipeline and the worst sim-to-real gap on the list; reacting to an obstacle is already covered blind, only anticipating one needs eyes.
